title: Conjecture 1.5
statement_text: Every sufficiently large integer is polite.
context_text: For a graph $H$ on $t$ vertices, $m(H,n)$ is the minimum number of monochromatic labeled copies of $H$ over all red/blue colorings of $E(K_n)$, and the Ramsey multiplicity constant is $c(H)=\lim_{n\to\infty}m(H,n)/(n)_t$, where $(n)_t=n(n-1)\cdots(n-t+1)$. A random coloring gives $c(H)\le 2^{1-e(H)}$ (graphs attaining this are called common). For $H$ connected with chromatic number $k$, the Turán coloring (red graph a disjoint union of $k-1$ balanced cliques, blue graph the complete $(k-1)$-partite graph) gives $c(H)\le(k-1)^{1-t}$. A connected graph $H$ is a (two-color) bonbon if, for all large $n$, the Turán coloring with $\chi(H)-1$ parts is, up to permuting colors and vertices, the unique coloring of $E(K_n)$ minimizing the number of monochromatic copies of $H$. For $q\ge3$ colors, $r_{q-1}(k)$ is the $(q-1)$-color Ramsey number of $K_k$, $r(a,b)$ is the two-color off-diagonal Ramsey number (least $r$ such that every red/blue coloring of $E(K_r)$ has a red $K_a$ or a blue $K_b$) and $r(k)=r(k,k)$; a Ramsey coloring of $K_{r(k)-1}$ is a red/blue coloring of its edges with no monochromatic $K_k$. A $q$-coloring of $E(K_n)$ is Ramsey-blowup-like if some color class is a disjoint union of $r_{q-1}(k)-1$ balanced cliques and the other colors contain no monochromatic $K_k$; a connected $t$-vertex graph $H$ with clique number $k$ is a $q$-color bonbon if for all large $n$ every $q$-coloring of $E(K_n)$ minimizing the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ is Ramsey-blowup-like (then $c_q(H)=(r_{q-1}(k)-1)^{1-t}$). A positive integer $k$ is polite if $r(k,\lceil k/2\rceil)\le 2^{-31}r(k,k)$ and $\frac{r(k,k)-1}{r(k,k-1)}\ge 1+25\left(\frac{r(k,\lceil k/2\rceil)}{r(k,k)}\right)^{1/4}$. The authors prove that if $k$ is a sufficiently large polite integer and $t$ is large enough in terms of $k$, then the graph obtained from $K_k$ by adding $t-k$ pendant edges is a 3-color bonbon; the conjecture would make this unconditional for all large $k$. It would follow from natural conjectures on the growth of Ramsey numbers: $r(k,\lceil k/2\rceil)=o(r(k,k))$, which gives the first inequality for large $k$, together with the Burr–Erdős conjecture $r(k,k)\ge(1+c)r(k,k-1)$ for an absolute $c>0$; but it seems out of reach, the best known lower bound on $r(k,k)-r(k,k-1)$ being far weaker.

title: Conjecture 5.3
statement_text: There exist a mixed blowup coloring of $K_{r(k)-1}[2]$ for infinitely many $k$.
context_text: The setting is Ramsey multiplicity: minimizing the number of monochromatic copies of a fixed graph $H$ over colorings of $E(K_n)$. For $q\ge3$ colors, $r_{q-1}(k)$ is the $(q-1)$-color Ramsey number of $K_k$, $r(a,b)$ is the two-color off-diagonal Ramsey number (least $r$ such that every red/blue coloring of $E(K_r)$ has a red $K_a$ or a blue $K_b$) and $r(k)=r(k,k)$; a Ramsey coloring of $K_{r(k)-1}$ is a red/blue coloring of its edges with no monochromatic $K_k$. A $q$-coloring of $E(K_n)$ is Ramsey-blowup-like if some color class is a disjoint union of $r_{q-1}(k)-1$ balanced cliques and the other colors contain no monochromatic $K_k$; a connected $t$-vertex graph $H$ with clique number $k$ is a $q$-color bonbon if for all large $n$ every $q$-coloring of $E(K_n)$ minimizing the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ is Ramsey-blowup-like (then $c_q(H)=(r_{q-1}(k)-1)^{1-t}$). For a graph $G$, $G[s]$ is its $s$-blowup (each vertex replaced by an independent set of $s$ vertices, each edge by a complete bipartite graph); here $K_{r(k)-1}[s]$ is the complete $(r(k)-1)$-partite graph with parts of size $s$. A mixed blowup coloring is a red/blue coloring of $E(K_{r(k)-1}[s])$ with no monochromatic $K_k$ that is not the blowup of a Ramsey coloring of $K_{r(k)-1}$. Mixed blowup colorings would show that, in the 3-color case, the Ramsey-blowup coloring is not the unique extremizer (any of them can serve as the red/blue part of an equally good 3-coloring), which is why $q$-color bonbons are defined via Ramsey-blowup-like colorings. The authors show that a mixed blowup coloring of $K_{r(k)-1}[2]$ exists if and only if one exists for every $s\ge2$, if and only if some 2-coloring of $E(K_{r(k)-2})$ extends to two distinct Ramsey colorings of $K_{r(k)-1}$. They cannot do this for any $k$: $r(k)$ is known only for $k=3,4$, and for both the Ramsey coloring of $K_{r(k)-1}$ is unique with all vertices of equal red and blue degree. They expect special values of $k$ with a unique structured (e.g. Paley) Ramsey coloring, hence conjecture existence only for infinitely many $k$; for the off-diagonal case $r(3,4)=9$ such colorings exist.

title: Conjecture 5.4
statement_text: If $k\geq 4$ and $t$ is sufficiently large in terms of $k$, then any $(k,t)$-generalized lollipop is a two-color bonbon.
context_text: For a graph $H$ on $t$ vertices, $m(H,n)$ is the minimum number of monochromatic labeled copies of $H$ over all red/blue colorings of $E(K_n)$, and the Ramsey multiplicity constant is $c(H)=\lim_{n\to\infty}m(H,n)/(n)_t$, where $(n)_t=n(n-1)\cdots(n-t+1)$. A random coloring gives $c(H)\le 2^{1-e(H)}$ (graphs attaining this are called common). For $H$ connected with chromatic number $k$, the Turán coloring (red graph a disjoint union of $k-1$ balanced cliques, blue graph the complete $(k-1)$-partite graph) gives $c(H)\le(k-1)^{1-t}$. A connected graph $H$ is a (two-color) bonbon if, for all large $n$, the Turán coloring with $\chi(H)-1$ parts is, up to permuting colors and vertices, the unique coloring of $E(K_n)$ minimizing the number of monochromatic copies of $H$. A graph is $k$-critical (in the paper's convention) if it has chromatic number $k$ and some edge whose deletion lowers the chromatic number. A $(k,t)$-generalized lollipop is a graph on $t$ vertices containing a $K_k$ whose deletion leaves a forest, i.e. $K_k$ with trees comprising $t-k$ vertices attached to its vertices; for such graphs the Turán coloring gives $c(H)\le(k-1)^{1-t}$. The authors prove that adding $t-h$ pendant edges to a $k$-critical graph $H_0$ on $h$ vertices yields a bonbon when $k\ge4$ and $t\ge(1000kh)^{10}h^{10k}$; their technique needs $t$ at least exponential in $k$, and for $H_0=K_k$ some lower bound is necessary since adding $o(k^2/\log k)$ pendant edges does not give a bonbon (the random coloring is better). The conjecture extends this from pendant edges to arbitrary attached trees. They also single out the special case of the lollipop $L_{k,t}$ ($K_k$ with a path of $t-k$ edges attached at one vertex), and ask whether, for $H_0=K_k$, $t$ polynomial in $k$ suffices.

title: Conjecture 5.5
statement_text: If $k\geq 4$ and $t$ is sufficiently large in terms of $k$, then $L_{k,t}$ is a two-color bonbon.
context_text: The lollipop graph $L_{k,t}$ is obtained from $K_k$ by appending to a single vertex a path with $t-k$ edges. This is a natural special case of Conjecture 5.4 (taking $H_0=K_k$), which the authors suggest may be easier to prove than the full conjecture.
